newsitem.title: INDIA: FII investments in 6 India firms need approval - RBI.
newsitem.headline: FII investments in 6 India firms need approval - RBI.

text.p: Fresh purchases by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in six Indian firms would need the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) prior approval, the RBI said in a statement on Saturday.
This was because FII holdings in the firms have reached the 20 percent "alert" limit, it said.
The six companies are: W.S. Industries Ltd, WSL Industries Ltd, PVD Plast Mould Ltd, Essel Packaging Ltd, Max India Ltd and Carrier Aircon Ltd.
The ceiling on FII holdings in a firm is 24 percent.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram raised this limit to 30 percent in his budget for fiscal 1997/98 beginning April 1, but this will become effective only after parliament approves the proposal, an RBI official said.
